check_description: This check verifies that `market_overview.tex` shows the NZ shell-egg market split into four distinct channels with all four quantified. (a) Foodservice and industrial appear as separate, named channels. (b) Retail grocery shown within the acceptable band. (c) Four-channel cut preserved: retail grocery / foodservice / industrial / direct (direct not collapsed). (d) all four channels carry numeric volume-share values approximately summing to 100%.
score_0_criteria: Any of: foodservice and industrial lumped into a single 'foodservice' or 'wholesale' bucket; or retail's share shown well below 65% or above 80%; or direct collapsed into another channel without explicit treatment; or the depiction shows fewer than 3 distinct channels; or (d-failure) only retail is quantified while foodservice / industrial / direct appear as labels without specific numeric values; or (d-failure) one or more of foodservice / industrial / direct is shown materially outside the acceptable band (foodservice outside 12-18%, industrial outside 7-13%, direct outside 1-5%); or (d-failure) the four channel values fail to approximately sum to ~95-105%.
score_1_criteria: All four conditions met: (a) foodservice and industrial appear as separate, named channels; (b) retail grocery shown as ~70-75% of volume (or equivalent quantitative anchor 65-80%) per Calthorpe Part 1 [00:05:08]: 'retail grocery is the big one ... somewhere around 70-75% of total NZ volume'; (c) the four-channel cut (retail / foodservice / industrial / direct) is preserved without lumping; Calthorpe explicitly distinguishes industrial from foodservice ('this is where I'd push back on people who lump it with foodservice'); and (d) all four channels are quantified with specific numeric volume-share values that approximately sum to ~95-105%; retail ~70-75% (band 65-80%), foodservice ~15% (band ~12-18%), industrial ~10% (band ~7-13%), direct ~2-3% (band ~1-5%) per Calthorpe Part 1 [00:05:08-00:06:42].

shared/transcript_industry_expert_part1.pdf (Calthorpe Part 1):
  [00:05:08-00:06:42]: 'Four channels properly. Retail grocery is the big one - Foodstuffs banners, that's Pak'nSave and New World, plus Woolworths NZ, that's Countdown. They're a clear duopoly, somewhere around 70-75% of total NZ volume goes through retail grocery. ... Then foodservice - that's restaurants, cafes, hotels, hospitality. Probably 15% of volume. Then industrial - and this is where I'd push back on people who lump it with foodservice - industrial is bakeries, mayonnaise manufacturers, food processors. Those are different customers, different channels, different prices. Industrial is maybe 10% of volume but with very different unit economics. Then "direct" - farmgate sales, farmer's markets, DTC subscriptions - is a rounding error, maybe 2-3% of volume.'
  [00:06:48]: 'Definitely separate. Different price discipline, different contract structures.'

check_description:
This check verifies that submitted `market_overview.tex` and `market_overview.pdf` form a clean single-page artefact on a standard page size with minimal on-page text and no render failures.
(Graderside quality gate; no source-pool files.); (a) `.tex` compiles cleanly via pdflatex and matches the submitted `.pdf`. (b) Output is exactly one page and uses a standard page geometry within the acceptable range. (c) On-page intro text is minimal with no body-text paragraphs. (d) No render-integrity failures; labels do not overlap, no clipping at page edges, legible at standard zoom.
score_0_criteria: Any of: .tex fails to compile or produces output that does not match the submitted .pdf; or output spans more than one page; or the page geometry exceeds A3 (paperwidth > 420mm or paperheight > 420mm); i.e. oversized custom geometry cramming multi-page content onto one logical page; or introductory text exceeds 2 sentences or contains body-text paragraphs / written brief; or rendered output has visible render-integrity failures (overlap, clipping, illegibility) at multiple points.
score_1_criteria: All of: (a) submitted .tex compiles cleanly via pdflatex and produces output matching the submitted .pdf; (b) output is a single page and the page geometry is within the A4-to-A3 range (paperwidth <= 420mm and paperheight <= 420mm); A4, US Letter, or A3 (portrait or landscape) all satisfy; (c) introductory text is <= 2 sentences with no body-text paragraphs (T1 is a depiction, not a written brief); (d) no render-integrity failures; labels do not overlap, text is not clipped at page edges, labels are legible at standard zoom without requiring zoom-to-200%+ to read.
specific_file_locations: week/halberd_ic_preread_template.docx Section 3.1 Market Overview verbatim: 'Source format: LaTeX with TikZ. Submit the .tex source alongside the compiled PDF.' 'Compiled output: The .pdf must derive from the submitted .tex - we recompile-check on submission.' 'A maximum of one or two sentences of introductory text is permitted; the rest of the deliverable is the figure itself.' Section 3.1 mandates a single-page LaTeX-TikZ market overview with both `market_overview.tex` (compilable source) and `market_overview.pdf` (rendered output) submitted. The page-geometry guardrails (A4 / US Letter / A3 within the A4-to-A3 paperwidth/paperheight range) are graderside engineering defaults derived from 'standard page size' professional appendix norms; they enforce the template's 'single page' requirement against the gaming case of oversized custom paperwidth/paperheight.

check_description: This check verifies that `market_overview.tex` uses the exact regulatory housing labels from the MPI/NAWAC Animal Welfare (Layer Hens) Code of Welfare 2018, avoids non-regulatory / marketing / American synonyms for those housing systems, keeps marketing tiers separate from housing systems, and annotates the colony cohort's end-2027 retailer-led phase-out. Where a source provides only a producer-level cage-free aggregate (barn + free-range combined), the compliant representation labels it 'barn + free-range' with the undisclosed split noted; 'cage-free' must not itself appear as a housing-system category label and may appear only as retailer-pledge / shelf-status framing. The registered company name 'Henergy Cage Free' is a proper noun and never counts as a violation.
score_0_criteria: Any of: (a) free-range labelled with marketing tier name ('pasture-raised', 'organic', 'cage-free'); or (b) barn labelled with non-regulatory term ('aviary', 'litter system') or collapsed with free-range under 'cage-free'; or (c) colony labelled with non-regulatory term ('enriched cage' as primary label, 'conventional'); or (d) a marketing tier (pasture-raised / organic / omega-3) presented as a separate primary housing system alongside free-range / barn / colony; a 4th category at the same level; without distinguishing it as a tier within free-range; or (e) colony presented as a stable / persistent housing category with no end-2027 phase-out annotation, transition arrow, or callout tying it to the retailer-led Phase 2 deadline; even if the deadline appears elsewhere on the page, the colony category itself must visibly carry the transition context; or (f-failure) any forbidden substitution appears as a primary housing-system label; 'cage free' or 'cage-free' used in place of 'barn' / 'free-range' / 'colony' as the category label (acceptable only as the retailer-pledge / shelf-status framing); or 'cage-free' introduced as a legend / category label for an aggregated barn + free-range block (the compliant label is 'barn + free-range, split not disclosed'); or 'free range' written without hyphen as the system label; or 'caged' used as a standalone housing-system label replacing 'colony' or 'colony cage'; or 'enriched cage' used as the primary colony-system label in place of 'colony' / 'colony cage'.
score_1_criteria: All six pass: (a) 'free-range' (hyphenated) used for the free-range housing system; verbatim regulatory term from nz_free_range_info_sheet.pdf title 'UNDERSTANDING NEW ZEALAND FREE-RANGE EGG FARMING'; (b) 'barn' used for the barn housing system per nz_barn_info_sheet.pdf 'A barn egg is laid by a hen in an indoor barn environment that does not contain cages'; (c) 'colony' or 'colony cage' used for the colony housing system per nz_colony_info_sheet.pdf 'A colony cage is an enlarged, inside enclosure that can house up to 60 hens'; (d) marketing tiers (pasture-raised, organic, omega-3) not presented as separate primary housing systems alongside free-range / barn / colony; either omitted from primary segmentation, or shown clearly as tiers within free-range with explicit visual or textual distinction (per Vivian Holst, #albatross-deal 2026-05-05 ts 1778002200: 'MPI's four housing systems are the primary cut (free-range, barn, colony, conventional cage). Pasture-raised, organic, and omega-3 are marketing tiers - they sit on top of free-range housing, not alongside it. Don't present them as separate primary housing systems in the deck. If we need to surface the premium dynamics, show them as sub-tiers within free-range with a clear visual or textual distinction. The four MPI labels are the structural taxonomy.'); (e) colony cohort annotated with end-2027 retailer-led Phase 2 phase-out context per Calthorpe Part 1 [00:07:31] 'The supermarket pledges to be cage-free by end of 2027 - both Foodstuffs and Woolworths NZ have committed publicly - have driven a lot of conversion ahead of the deadline' (annotation on colony category, transition arrow to barn / free-range with end-2027 deadline, or callout tying colony to Foodstuffs + Woolworths NZ end-2027 commitments); and (f) none of the following forbidden non-regulatory / marketing / American substitutions appear in `market_overview.tex` as housing-system labels on the page: 'cage free' or 'cage-free' used as a primary housing-system label (acceptable only as retailer-pledge / shelf-status framing such as 'cage-free shelf by end-2027'); where sources give only producer-level cage-free aggregates (Calthorpe Part 2 [00:32:10], e.g. 'Mainland is now closer to 85%', 'they're maybe 45-50% cage-free' (Heyden), 'Better Eggs is 65%. Zeagold is 70-75%.'), an aggregate block labelled 'barn + free-range (split not disclosed)' passes while a legend or category labelled 'cage-free' fails; the company name 'Henergy Cage Free' never counts; 'free range' written without hyphen as the system label; 'caged' as a standalone housing-system label; 'enriched cage' used as the primary system label in place of 'colony' or 'colony cage'. Minor capitalisation variants acceptable; the hyphen in 'free-range' is required.

check_description: This check verifies that `market_overview.tex` depicts the NZ shell-egg value chain end-to-end with Aurora positioned, annotates margin-capture/buyer-power dynamics, quantifies retailer-side margin in per-dozen terms, and names the Foodstuffs vs Woolworths NZ buyer-power asymmetry. (a) Value chain depicted end-to-end: producer -> grading/wholesale/distribution -> retail and foodservice end-points, with Aurora positioned along it. (b) Relative margin-capture or buyer-power dynamics annotated across stages. (c) Retailer-side margin capture quantified in absolute per-dozen dollars (not just generic labels or percentage bands without dollar anchors). Producer margin only (without retailer capture) fails (c). (d) Foodstuffs vs Woolworths NZ buyer-power asymmetry named with structural distinction between the two retailers' buying models. Both retailers named without their structures distinguished fails (d).
score_0_criteria: Any of: value chain not depicted end-to-end (missing wholesale / grading / distribution intermediary stages or missing retail / foodservice end-points or Aurora not positioned along it); or (b) margin-capture / buyer-power dynamics not annotated at all (stages shown but no relative scale, no wholesale-to-retail uplift, no buyer-power asymmetry); or (c-failure) retailer-side margin capture not quantified in absolute per-dozen terms; depiction shows only generic 'high margin' / 'low margin' labels or only percentage bands without the NZ$5.40 gate / NZ$8.50 shelf / ~NZ$2.00 net contribution anchors; or (c-failure) producer margin quantified but retailer capture omitted; or (d-failure) Foodstuffs and Woolworths NZ named together without distinguishing their structurally different buying models (co-op / two-layer vs centralised single-buyer); or (d-failure) buyer-power named generically across 'the major retailers' without separating Foodstuffs from Woolworths NZ.
score_1_criteria: All four: (a) value chain depicted end-to-end (producer -> wholesale / grading / distribution intermediaries -> retail and foodservice end-points) with Aurora's positioning shown along it; (b) relative margin-capture or buyer-power dynamics annotated across stages; (c) retailer-side margin capture quantified explicitly in absolute per-dozen terms; NZ$5.40 wholesale gate (band ~NZ$5.20-5.60) and NZ$8.50 retail shelf (band ~NZ$8.00-9.00) for a standard free-range dozen, with retailer net margin shown as either ~22-28% of shelf or ~NZ$2.00 net contribution per dozen, per Calthorpe Part 4 [00:01:10]: 'The producer is selling that dozen to the retailer at a wholesale gate price of around NZ$5.20 to NZ$5.60 - call it NZ$5.40 mid-point' and [00:02:38]: 'Net retailer margin on free-range eggs is typically 22 to 28% of shelf - call it about NZ$2.00 of net contribution per dozen'; (d) Foodstuffs vs Woolworths NZ buyer-power asymmetry named with structural distinction visible per Calthorpe Part 4 [00:12:50] 'Foodstuffs is a co-operative ... two-layer buying structure' vs [00:14:18] 'Woolworths NZ ... single corporate retailer with a centralised distribution network ... single buyer per category'; or explicit ~3-5pp additional Woolworths NZ producer-side margin compression called out per [00:16:48]: 'Woolworths NZ extracts roughly 3 to 5 percentage points more producer-side margin compression than Foodstuffs'.

shared/transcript_industry_expert_part4.pdf (Calthorpe Part 4):
  [00:01:10]: 'Take a standard dozen of free-range eggs that retails at NZ$8.50 in a Pak'nSave or Countdown today. The producer is selling that dozen to the retailer at a wholesale gate price of around NZ$5.20 to NZ$5.60 - call it NZ$5.40 mid-point... So the producer is making maybe 65 to 85 cents of EBITDA per dozen on free-range. That is a 12 to 16% EBITDA margin.'
  [00:02:38]: 'On a NZ$5.40 gate to NZ$8.50 shelf - the retailer captures NZ$3.10 of gross margin per dozen, before their own shrink, labour, store overhead, distribution. Net retailer margin on free-range eggs is typically 22 to 28% of shelf - call it about NZ$2.00 of net contribution per dozen. So in absolute dollars the retailer makes more EBITDA per dozen than the producer does. About 2.5x more.'
  [00:03:30]: 'Retail in NZ is structurally the highest-margin step.'
  [00:08:18]: 'Foodservice channel is different. Aurora doesn't sell direct to a thousand cafes. They sell to foodservice wholesalers - Bidfood is the dominant one, then Gilmours - and the wholesaler delivers to the operator. The wholesaler takes a 12 to 18% margin on top of the gate price.'
  [00:10:24]: 'Industrial is a separate animal again. Bakeries, mayonnaise manufacturers, food processors. They buy bulk - sometimes liquid egg, sometimes shell. Liquid is processed by a dedicated breaker plant... Producer gate for industrial shell is NZ$3.20 to NZ$3.60 per dozen - thinnest gate of any channel. Breaker takes another 10 to 15% on top.'
  [00:12:50]: 'Foodstuffs is a co-operative - Foodstuffs North Island and Foodstuffs South Island, two separate co-ops with separate boards, plus Foodstuffs Own Brands Limited which manages the Pams, Pams Value, Pams Finest national private-label programme. The individual store - your local Pak'nSave, your local New World - is owner-operated, and the owner has discretion on local-supplier ranging within the national framework. So when a producer signs with Foodstuffs, they're signing with a national category buyer who handles the Pams private-label tender, but the owner-operators have shelf-space discretion on branded SKUs. It's a two-layer buying structure.'
  [00:14:18]: 'Woolworths NZ - that's Countdown, rebranded - is a single corporate retailer with a centralised distribution network. Their buying is fully national, single buyer per category, no store-level discretion to speak of... when you sign with Woolworths NZ you're signing one contract for all Countdown stores nationally. That gives them more leverage than Foodstuffs in any single negotiation - one decision delists you nationally.'
  [00:16:48]: 'Woolworths NZ extracts roughly 3 to 5 percentage points more producer-side margin compression than Foodstuffs, in steady-state, because of that single-buyer leverage.'
  [00:17:36]: Aurora retail mix '55-60% of retail volume into Foodstuffs banners across both islands, 35-40% into Woolworths NZ Countdown stores, residual to Costco NZ and a couple of independents. Foodstuffs-tilted is the better commercial position to be in.'

check_description:
This check verifies that `market_overview.tex` (and the compiled `market_overview.pdf`) complies with two firm-wide Halberd conventions: (a) the no-recommendation rule, and (b) US English spelling.

The deliverable must verify all of:
(a) No explicit invest / pass / continue-diligence recommendation language and no thesis-pillar framing in the title, intro, captions, or annotations. The rule is firm-wide per standards Section 9 and IC pre-read template Section 4 Hard Rules; both sources prohibit a recommendation position in any preliminary deliverable.
(b) US English spelling throughout the .tex source and the rendered .pdf body text (caption text, axis labels, intro sentence, TikZ annotations). Halberd is a US private-equity firm; US English is the implicit firm-wide convention. Any single instance of British / Commonwealth spelling fails this sub-criterion - e.g., 'realise' instead of 'realize', 'organise', 'colour', 'centre', 'programme', 'analyse', 'favour', 'behaviour', 'specialise'. Proper-noun spellings retain their canonical form (e.g., 'World Organisation for Animal Health' / WOAH, registered company names, official department names) and do not count as fails. LaTeX command names (e.g., `\colorbox`, `\centering`) are markup tokens, not authored prose, and do not count as fails either.

All sub-criteria must pass; failure on any one fails the check.
score_0_criteria: Any of: (a) explicit recommendation phrase present ('we recommend invest', 'we recommend pass', 'continue diligence', 'we should proceed', 'bid at X', equivalent); or thesis-pillar framing present as a structural element (slide heading, title, callout, or summary block using 'compelling opportunity' / 'attractive asset' / 'strong fit for the platform' / equivalent thesis-style framing); or (b) any single instance of British or Commonwealth spelling in the .tex source's or rendered .pdf's authored prose (excluding proper nouns / registered org names / LaTeX command names) - e.g., realise, organise, colour, centre, programme, analyse, favour, behaviour, specialise, kilometre, defence, licence (when used as a verb); one instance is enough to fail.
score_1_criteria: All of: (a) the .tex source and compiled .pdf contain no explicit invest / pass / continue-diligence recommendation language and no thesis-pillar / 'compelling fit' / 'attractive opportunity' / 'strong platform fit' framing as a structural element (slide heading, title, callout, or thesis-style summary block); neutral descriptive use of words like 'attractive' embedded in prose (e.g. 'attractive entry multiple') is acceptable provided it is not framed as a thesis pillar; (b) every word of authored prose in the .tex source and the rendered .pdf uses US English spelling; proper nouns and registered organisation names retain canonical spelling and do not count as fails; LaTeX command names are markup tokens and do not count as fails.

no-recommendation rule (sub-criterion (a)):
Standards doc Section 9 (Deal-Stage Principles and Recommendation Discipline), §9.2 Recommendation Discipline closes with: 'No "invest" / "pass" / "continue diligence" verdict in any preliminary deliverable - pure assessment'. IC pre-read template Section 4 Hard Rules: 'No recommendations. Pre-LOI deliverables are a preliminary assessment for the IC - not an IC pitch. Decks, videos, or memos taking a recommendation position (proceed / pass / bid at X) will be rejected. Findings, risks, and open questions only.'

US English spelling (sub-criterion (b)): no single explicit spelling directive is planted, but the Halberd-authored corpus consistently uses US English (brand guidelines, analytical standards, IC pre-read template, compliance handbook, internal Slack), while NZ third-party sources retain Commonwealth spelling; the firm-wide written convention is inferable from the corpus. Applies to the .tex source and the compiled .pdf body text (caption text, axis labels, intro sentence, annotations on the TikZ diagram).

The contradiction with Calthorpe Part 1's current-era 40/40/20 read still holds. check_description:
Pairwise comparison: which `market_overview.tex` (rendered to `market_overview.pdf`) is the stronger single-page market-overview artefact across four analytical-quality dimensions distinct from any binary check in the rubric.

The four dimensions:
- (1) Source breadth and cross-referencing; distinct source count visibly cited in the depiction (footnotes, data labels, endnotes, in-place attributions), plus multi-source triangulation on the depiction's central numeric claims (producer shares, production-system mix, cage-free transition, retailer commitments) versus single-source reliance.
- (2) Data-quality caveats and framing; provenance / vintage flags on figures shown (e.g. FY25 actual vs FY26 forecast labelling; '2022-vintage' or 'as-of-2022 EPF baseline' tags on the stale-mix figures; 'as of' dates on time-sensitive data); sell-side framing tags on broker-sourced inputs (e.g. broker-asking 17-19% Aurora share flagged as sell-side, Calthorpe Part 2 18% flagged as the interview-refined working anchor); explicit handling of contradicting sources rather than silent averaging.
- (3) Explanation clarity and per-element analytical takeaway; legend / key / annotation readable; figures interpretable without external decoding (units, denominator, base-year stated in-line); the depiction's central analytical claim about market structure auditable from the on-page content alone. Distinct from P-01 which tests visual scannability (font size, layout, whitespace); this dimension tests whether the reader can audit the analytical claim from what's on the page.
- (4) Synthesis vs enumeration; the diagram tells the market structure story at a glance (producer concentration + channel structure + production-system transition arc) integrated into a coherent narrative, versus a flat collection of labelled boxes / numbers without prioritisation or causal / structural logic.

A stronger output addresses all four dimensions with concrete evidence. At least one observably stronger dimension with no material regression on the others determines the winner. Differences must be observable from the rendered PDF (and `.tex` source where source attributions sit in TikZ nodes). Surface complexity (more nodes, denser annotations) does not satisfy a dimension unless substantive analytical depth is present.
score_0_criteria: Output B is stronger across the same four dimensions (or strictly stronger on at least one with no regression). Outputs that rely on single-source citations for material claims, that present numbers as authoritative without provenance / vintage / sell-side framing, that show figures whose units / denominator / base-year are not auditable from the page, or that enumerate market elements without prioritisation or structural logic lose on the corresponding dimensions. Surface complexity (more nodes, denser annotations) does not satisfy a dimension unless substantive analytical depth is present. Where outputs are tied on a dimension, that dimension does not count toward either side.
score_1_criteria: Output A is stronger across the four dimensions, or strictly stronger on at least one with no regression on the others. Specifically: (1) deeper source breadth with distinct sources visibly cited in the depiction (footnotes / data labels / endnotes) and multi-source triangulation on central numeric claims (e.g. producer shares cross-cited Calthorpe + Hartley Pearce; production-system mix cross-cited Calthorpe Part 1 + EPF FY25) rather than single-source reliance; (2) explicit data-quality caveats and framing on material figures; vintage / 'as of' tags on time-sensitive data (FY25 actual vs FY26 forecast labelling; 2022-vintage flag on the stale 33/33/34 EPF baseline), sell-side framing tags on broker-sourced inputs, explicit reconciliation of contradicting sources; (3) reasoning chain visible from the on-page content; units / denominator / base-year stated in-line, legend / key readable, the central analytical claim auditable from the depiction alone without external lookup; (4) prioritised synthesis; the diagram integrates producer concentration + channel structure + production-system transition into a coherent story rather than enumerating flat parallel boxes. Differences must be supportable from the rendered PDF (and `.tex` source where source attributions sit in TikZ nodes); surface complexity is not analytical depth.

check_description:
Pairwise comparison: which `market_overview.tex` (rendered to `market_overview.pdf`) produces a more polished, professional single-page CDD market-overview appendix artefact?

- (1) Node and label spacing. No overlapping shapes (nodes, boxes, containers physically overlapping each other on the rendered page); no overlapping labels; generous-enough whitespace that the eye can track grouping and direction without strain. Shape-on-shape overlap is the most penalised failure on this dimension - any visible overlap between two boxes / nodes / containers is treated as a near-automatic loss on dim (1) regardless of other spacing strengths. Arrows / lines / connectors do not overlap any text label or node body other than at their intended endpoints; no connectors crossing through node bodies or label boxes mid-path. Outputs that just barely avoid overlap score lower than outputs with comfortable margins.
- (2) Containment within shapes and bounds. Text inside coloured boxes, bounding shapes, and nodes does not overflow or clip; all elements sit within the page bounds without bleeding off edges; arrows and connectors stay inside the page bounds and do not visually clip on the page edge.
- (3) Typographic and line-weight consistency. Title differentiated from section labels; node labels at consistent size; consistent font family across the page (no mixed serif / sans, no random typeface substitutions); arrow / box / divider line weights coherent. Use of preset TikZ styles (`\tikzset`) or `\newcommand` macros for a consistent visual vocabulary is preferred over inline ad-hoc styling that varies element-by-element.
- (4) Visual design discipline and aesthetic restraint. Restrained institutional colour palette (a defined set of 3-6 semantically named colours applied consistently - e.g. a primary navy / accent gold / neutral grey palette) beats arbitrary use of default TikZ pastel fills (`yellow!20`, `orange!20`, `red!20`, `brown!10` etc. picked ad hoc by what looks 'fine'). Colour assignments should be semantic and consistent across the page (e.g. the colour used for 'colony' in the production-system column should match the colour used for 'colony' wherever else it appears). Penalties: default TikZ pastels applied without a defined palette; >6 distinct fill colours without semantic justification; clashing colour combinations; over-decorated pages with splashy fills that obscure the structural content; under-decorated monochrome pages that miss hierarchy entirely.
- (5) Information hierarchy. Clear visual hierarchy across at least four typographic / colour strata: title > section / column header > primary node label > secondary annotation / footnote. Each stratum is distinguishable by some combination of size, weight, and colour. Pages where everything sits at similar visual weight (flat hierarchy) score lower than pages where the eye is led through the content by deliberate size / weight / colour contrast.
- (6) Legend, key, and annotation completeness. Colour coding, fill / hatch patterns, and arrow conventions explained via a legible legend or in-place key; annotations carry units / sources / dates where required. Footnote formatting: where footnotes are used, they are formatted at the bottom of the page (not floating mid-page), set at a footnote-appropriate size smaller than body text (e.g. `\footnotesize` or smaller), do not overlap the diagram body or page edge, and footnote numbering / markers match the in-diagram superscripts / markers exactly.
- (7) Compilation-render fidelity. The submitted `.tex` recompiles to a PDF that is visually identical to the submitted `.pdf` (no missing TikZ libraries, no font fallbacks producing different glyphs, no silent diagram-component drops). A-02 gates clean compilation as a binary; this dimension judges fidelity-of-match between source and submitted render.
score_0_criteria: Output B is observably more polished across the same seven dimensions (or strictly stronger on at least one with no regression). Visual judgements must be supportable from the rendered PDF; surface density is not polish. Ties on a dimension do not count toward either side. Overlapping shapes (nodes, boxes, or containers physically overlapping each other on the rendered page) is a near-automatic loss on dim (1) for the offending output, regardless of other spacing strengths. Arrows / lines / connectors that cross through node bodies or text labels at non-endpoint moments lose on dim (1). Text or elements clipped or bleeding off the page edge lose on dim (2). Mixed font families (e.g. serif title with sans body, or random typeface substitutions) or inconsistent label sizing lose on dim (3). Default TikZ pastel fills (`yellow!20`, `orange!20`, `red!20`, `brown!10`) used as the primary palette without a defined institutional colour scheme, or >6 distinct fill colours without semantic justification, or inconsistent semantic colour assignment across columns / rows lose on dim (4). Flat visual hierarchy where title, section headers, and body labels are indistinguishable in size / weight / colour loses on dim (5). Footnotes that float mid-page, sit at body-text size or larger, overlap the diagram body, or carry numbering mismatched with in-diagram superscripts lose on dim (6). Recompiled `.tex` producing a PDF that differs materially from the submitted PDF (missing libraries, font fallbacks, dropped components) loses on dim (7).
score_1_criteria: Output A is observably more polished across the seven dimensions: (1) tighter node and label spacing with no overlapping shapes (any shape-on-shape overlap is a near-automatic loss on this dim), comfortable margins, arrows / connectors not crossing through node bodies or labels other than at intended endpoints; (2) cleaner containment within shapes and page bounds (no clipping, no off-page bleed, connectors stay inside page bounds); (3) more consistent typography, font family, and line weights (title differentiated, consistent label sizing, coherent line weights), with preset TikZ styles or `\newcommand` macros preferred over inline ad-hoc styling; (4) more disciplined visual design (defined institutional colour palette of 3-6 semantically named colours, consistent semantic colour assignment, restrained decoration) beating default TikZ pastels applied ad hoc; (5) clearer information hierarchy across title > section / column header > primary label > secondary annotation, distinguishable by size / weight / colour; (6) more complete legend / key / annotation coverage with proper footnote formatting; (7) stronger compilation-render fidelity (recompiled PDF matches the submitted PDF without missing libraries, font fallbacks, or dropped components). At least one dimension observably stronger and no dimension regresses materially. Visual judgements must be supportable from the rendered PDF.
